title: Variable Retention Harvest Explained
reason: Explains the variable retention harvest method and its ecological benefits for forest management.

tasks.task: Describe the variable retention harvest method and its ecological benefits.

subtasks.text: Observe the diverse forest management objectives, including timber production and habitat creation.
Note the difference between clear-cutting and thinning as reference points for understanding variable retention harvest.
Highlight the characteristics of clumps and individual trees left behind after harvesting in a variable retention method.
Explain the importance of maintaining habitat diversity through ecological forestry.
Identify the equipment used in variable retention harvest, such as cable systems and ground-based cut-to-length systems.

tasks.task: Illustrate how variable retention harvest imitates natural disturbances to benefit species diversity.

subtasks.text: Observe groups of trees, patches, and individual trees left behind in a patchy arrangement.
Note the variety of tree species and sizes left behind.
Highlight the goal of creating biodiversity by emulating natural disturbances.
Mention specific declining species that the habitat provides for, such as the Rufus Hummingbird and Orange Crown Warbler.
